diagnosis: Five observed stops were local worker60-second SIGALRM timers; exact logical request107 timed out on all three physical attempts107,108,109.

implementation_evidence.timer: SIGALRM/ITIMER_REAL=60; urllib socket timeout=60; outer supervisor request limit=62 and original total deadline
implementation_evidence.stream: Requests set stream=true, but worker reads the response body completely before parsing/saving. No partial SSE progress or time-to-first-byte is persisted.
implementation_evidence.exit_zero: Worker catches local Stop and writes an error envelope, then exits normally; exit0 is not a successful provider reply.

limitations: No persisted HTTP status, response body or usage exists for75,96,107,108,109. Cannot locate the stall in connect/headers/body, infer server cancellation, or distinguish queueing, generation and network delay.
Success-only latency statistics are censored by60 seconds and do not estimate the failed requests eventual completion times.
The approved identical-body retries76 and97 completed in34.485 and22.563 seconds; this is consistent with transient variability but does not identify its cause.
The client reads the entire stream before parsing. Without saved progress, cannot rule out waiting for EOF even if a terminal SSE event had arrived; no evidence shows that this happened.

recommendation.rationale: Allow twice the former client wait and more headroom above the observed54.825-second success tail;120 is an engineering bound, not an empirically established optimum or completion guarantee.
keep: bounded retries with backoff and unknown usage retained
recommendation.comparability: Changing the client wait would leave prompt and retrieval parameters unchanged, but changes which responses complete and would create a mixed timeout policy. Record the exact boundary; compare retrieval descriptively, and do not attribute improved completion, latency/cost or retrieval solely to prompt changes.
recommendation.exhausted_request: Changing the timer does not reset attempt count; this exhausted request needs a separately defined decision before any further replay.
recommendation.observability_for_next_authorized_attemp: Record only safe timing and byte/event counters for first byte, last progress and completed terminal event. This can distinguish slow generation from a stream that does not close; do not publish credentials or partial internal reasoning. No instrumentation change was applied here.

applied_change: Only authorized retries108 and109 with5/15-second backoff. No timeout, cumulative budget, deadline or prompt changes.
